chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Isma'il ibn al-Jabir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the creation and knew what they would return to. He commanded them and forbade them. Whatever He commanded them of anything, He made for them the way to take it; and whatever He forbade them from, He made for them the way to leave it. And they do not take or leave except by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and High, meaning: by His Knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine knowledge and human capability in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the position between compulsion and free will), asserting that while humans possess the inherent capacity (*qudra*) to act, their actualization is contingent upon divine permission. The Imam clarifies that 'permission' here denotes Allah’s comprehensive foreknowledge (*ilm*) rather than a causal constraint, thereby reconciling human agency with divine omniscience. This serves as a foundational text for understanding how created beings are accountable for their choices within the scope of God’s decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, on the authority of Isma`il ibn al-Jabir, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created a creation and knew they will not proceed to Him. He command them what they should o, and what they should not do. He never commands people to do something, unless He gives them the means to do it. And He never commanded people to refrain from doing something unless He gives them the means from refraining from it. People never obey or disobey but by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and High, i.e. with His Knowledge.
